newsitem.title: USA: Motorola Q4 may show hints of rebound - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Motorola Q4 may show hints of rebound - analysts.

text.p: A slight improvement in Motorola Inc's semiconductor business and hints of an upturn in wireless phone sales may add a glimmer of hope to the dismal fourth quarter results expected to be reported by the technology giant Thursday, analysts said.

Motorola said it will report fourth quarter earnings after the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange on Thursday, sometime after 1600 EST (2100 GMT). Analysts expect them to be some 43 percent below last year.

According to First Call, the consensus of analysts' 1996 fourth quarter earnings estimates is $0.41 a share, compared with the $0.72 a share earned last year. The earnings decline for the quarter would be the third in a row for the company.

Mona Eraiba, an analyst for Gruntal & Co, said she sees Motorola's wireless business and semiconductors showing improvement from the third quarter despite the lower year-ago earnings comparisons. Motorola earned $0.34 in the third quarter versus $0.81 last year.
"I don't see why it won't be somewhat better than third quarter," Eraiba said.
The company is expected to report charges related to cost cutting and layoffs in its semiconductor and other businesses.
"The bigger the charge, the happier I am," Eraiba said, adding that would mean aggressive changes and cost cutting.
